shifts.summary: The shift was overall reported as moderate. Reasoning was mixed, with many diagram and statement questions and no coding‑decoding types. GA was generally easy, covering current affairs and constitutional articles. Quant was lengthy with heavy data‑interpretation and arithmetic, causing time pressure. English was the hardest section, featuring long comprehension and vocabulary items.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Candidates reported a mix of easy and moderate difficulty, noting many diagram‑based and statement questions and the absence of coding‑decoding types. Some found the paper lengthy and skipped a few items due to time pressure.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: GK was generally reported as easy or okay, with current affairs and history items and some logical fixed‑answer questions. Candidates found it doable.

topics.topic: Article 3 – power to alter state boundaries

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Candidates found math hard and lengthy, with many calculative DI and geometry questions. Time pressure was high, leading to skipping strategies and difficulty completing within the allotted time.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: English was reported as difficult with lengthy comprehension and vocabulary items, though spelling questions were easier. Some candidates found the passage easy and attempted all questions.

observations: Overall paper was moderate, but math and English sections were harder for many candidates.
Time pressure was a common issue, especially in quant and reasoning.
Good attempts varied, with overall range 60–82 and section ranges reflecting difficulty.
Many diagram‑based reasoning and extensive data‑interpretation questions were noted.

intro: The SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam held on 14 October 2026 was reported as moderate overall across the first two shifts. Reasoning questions included a mix of diagram and statement items, while General Awareness focused on current affairs and constitutional articles. Quantitative Aptitude was lengthy with heavy data‑interpretation and arithmetic, creating time pressure, and English was noted as the most challenging section. All figures mentioned are unofficial, and SSC normalises scores across shifts.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty level of the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 14 October 2026?
faqs.a: Both reported shifts on 14 October 2026 described the paper as moderate in difficulty. The third shift is still pending, so no overall assessment is available for it yet.

faqs.q: How was the Reasoning section perceived in the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 14 October 2026?
faqs.a: Candidates noted a mixed difficulty for Reasoning on 14 October 2026, with many diagram and statement questions. The first shift leaned toward moderate, while the second shift ranged from easy to moderate.

faqs.q: What challenges did candidates face in the Quantitative Aptitude section on 14 October 2026?
faqs.a: Quantitative Aptitude was described as lengthy and heavy on data‑interpretation and arithmetic, leading to time pressure. The difficulty was generally moderate, with some reports indicating a shift toward moderate‑to‑difficult.

faqs.q: How did candidates rate the General Awareness (GA) section on 14 October 2026?
faqs.a: GA was largely seen as easy, covering current affairs and constitutional articles, though some candidates reported a range from easy to moderate and up to moderate‑to‑difficult in the second shift.
